title: Improved Visualization of the Internal Branch of the Superior Laryngeal Nerve during Pharyngeal Endoscopic Subepithelial Dissection with Use of Red Dichromatic Imaging

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Improved Visualization of the Internal Branch of the Superior Laryngeal Nerve during Pharyngeal Endoscopic Subepithelial Dissection with Use of Red Dichromatic Imaging》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · deo270460-sec-0010-p1】Superficial pharyngeal cancers have been increasingly detected at an early stage through widespread image‐enhancing endoscopy. Techniques for removing these tumors may be minimally invasive and may preserve laryngeal and swallowing function. Endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) has become widely adopted for superficial pharyngeal cancer because it enables preservation of organ function and has demonstrated efficacy and safety [1].

【Introduction · deo270460-sec-0010-p2】Unlike gastrointestinal ESD, pharyngeal ESD presents unique anatomical challenges, including a narrow field, vascular and neural structures such as the internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve (ibSLN) within the subepithelial layer, and underlying muscle or cartilage in some regions [2, 3]. Therefore, structures must be accurately identified intraoperatively, and dissection must be performed with caution to avoid structural injury, particularly nerve damage. Injury to nerves may cause dysphagia and hoarseness, which adversely affect postoperative quality of life [4, 5].

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Improved Visualization of the Internal Branch of the Superior Laryngeal Nerve during Pharyngeal Endoscopic Subepithelial Dissection with Use of Red Dichromatic Imaging》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Case Report · deo270460-sec-0020-p2】The EVIS X1 endoscopy system (Olympus, Tokyo, Japan) with GIF‐XZ1200 and GIF‐H290T endoscopes (Olympus) was used during the dissection. While the patient was under general anesthesia, we exposed the operative field using a Sato curved laryngoscope. After initial evaluation of the lesion with narrow‐band imaging (Figure 1a), WLI (Figure 1b) depicted a whitish linear structure beneath the lesion; because of its anatomical location and course, we assumed that it represented the ibSLN. RDI mode 1 depicted the presumed nerve more clearly as a white linear structure (Figure 1c). After local submucosal injection of hyaluronic acid, the nerve remained more clearly visible with RDI than with WLI despite adequate subepithelial elevation (Figure 2). After circumferential mucosal incision adjacent to the nerve, the nerve remained unclear with WLI but was clearer with RDI (Figure 3a,b). During the subsequent subepithelial dissection, RDI also delineated the boundary between the presumed nerve and the surrounding subepithelial tissue more clearly than did WLI (Figure 3c,d); this enhanced visualization may have helped guide identification of the dissection plane. A FlushKnife BTs 2.0 (DK2618JB20; Fujifilm Corporation, Tokyo, Japan) was used for dissection. Two milliliters of hyaluronic acid were injected into the submucosal layer. The lesion was successfully resected en bloc within 12 min, without bleeding or nerve injury (Figure 4). The procedure was performed by an endoscopist with experience in approximately 30 pharyngeal and 100 esophageal ESD procedures. Histopathological examination revealed high‐grade dysplasia with negative resection margins. During regular postoperative follow‐up, including laryngoscopic examinations, no adverse events, including dysphagia, hoarseness, or impairment of the swallowing or cough reflexes, were observed. No such abnormalities have been identified during the 10‐month follow‐up period to date.

【Discussion · deo270460-sec-0030-p3】In our patient, a whitish linear structure considered to represent the ibSLN was identifiable under conventional WLI. Under RDI, however, the structure was visualized more clearly as a distinct white linear structure, which may have facilitated its intraoperative identification. Importantly, the presumed nerve could be visualized before and after submucosal injection for subepithelial elevation, which may have helped guide the circumferential mucosal incision and subepithelial dissection while maintaining an appropriate dissection plane and avoiding apparent nerve injury.

sections.title: 图表阅读
sections.text:
《Improved Visualization of the Internal Branch of the Superior Laryngeal Nerve during Pharyngeal Endoscopic Subepithelial Dissection with Use of Red Dichromatic Imaging》：图表的原始标题与说明。

【FIGURE 1 · deo270460-fig-0001】FIGURE 1 (a) Narrow‐band imaging depicted a 5‐mm brownish area on the pharyngoepiglottic fold (indicated by the red circle). (b) White‐light imaging depicted a whitish linear structure, which was presumed to be the internal branch of the superior laryngeal nerve based on its anatomical location and expected course. (c) Red dichromatic imaging demonstrated the nerve more clearly as a white linear structure.

【FIGURE 2 · deo270460-fig-0002】FIGURE 2 Comparison of white‐light imaging (WLI) (a) and red dichromatic imaging (RDI) (b) after submucosal injection of hyaluronic acid. Even after subepithelial elevation induced by the injection, the nerve appeared whiter and was more clearly visible with RDI than with WLI.

【FIGURE 3 · deo270460-fig-0003】FIGURE 3 Comparison of white‐light imaging (WLI) (a) and red dichromatic imaging (RDI) (b) during endoscopic subepithelial dissection after circumferential mucosal incision. During subepithelial dissection, the nerve was less clearly visualized with WLI, but it was more clearly visualized with RDI. With RDI, the surrounding tissue appeared blue to gray due to the blue injection solution, providing greater contrast with the whitish nerve and facilitating identification of its course. The arrowheads indicate the nerve. The nerve was identifiable with both WLI (c) and RDI (d); however, the whitish appearance of the nerve was more prominent with RDI than with WLI.
